content: Religious fasting practices, such as those observed during Ramadan and Yom Kippur, require individuals to abstain from food and drink for specific periods of time. For individuals with diabetes who choose to participate in these fasts, it is essential to provide education on how to effectively manage their blood glucose levels during the fasting period. This includes guidance on adjusting their medications appropriately and maintaining safe levels of physical activity to prevent complications. Healthcare professionals should offer tailored recommendations that take into account the specific type of diabetes the individual has, as well as the duration and nature of the fasting period. This personalized approach ensures that the individual can observe their religious practices while minimizing health risks associated with fasting.
